items.subject: ELA
items.finding: Teacher-published practice keys conflate phrases with dependent clauses in some items.
items.example: After the storm, the dogs went for a run.
items.correctTeaching: After the storm is a prepositional phrase, with no subject–verb pair. The sentence has one independent clause and is simple. Keep the correct clause test; the presence of after alone does not make a sentence complex.
items.parentAction: Have Ry identify the subject and verb before classifying. Clarify the key discrepancy with the teacher or tutor. This is a source issue, not an observed fresh error by Ry.

items.subject: Social Studies
items.finding: Assigned Egypt sources use different hierarchy groupings and contain historical errors.
items.correctTeaching: Anchor any hierarchy question to its named diagram. Hatshepsut was not the earliest female ruler; the Great Sphinx is at Giza, not the Valley of the Kings. Do not copy textbook errors into factual answer keys.
items.parentAction: Use the actual required project diagram and confirm conflicts rather than assuming one universal chart.

items.subject: Theatre
items.finding: The teacher music collection includes both instrumentals and lyrical tracks. One displayed lyric description includes profanity.
items.parentAction: Review the teacher choices; instrumental selections are already present. No mime rubric or due date has been posted.

items.subject: Science dates
items.finding: Some published daily pages retain2025 weekday/date wording inside2026 folders. These are date conflicts, not confirmed new deadlines.
items.correctTeaching: Keep the October30 newsletter’s November6 guided-notes deadline and November10 Ecology vocabulary quiz. Do not convert copied future day/date labels into calendar events.
items.parentAction: Confirm later Ecology/Biomes assessment and project dates from a current teacher update. Resource availability does not establish its due date.

items.subject: Social Studies project
items.finding: The major-project introduction and writing rubric request one in-class paragraph, while the mummy-option slide says two paragraphs.
items.parentAction: Confirm the paragraph count for the selected option. The project is due December2 and the teacher says no early projects. The visual is desktop-sized; visual and in-class writing are each50points.

items.subject: Social Studies
items.finding: Current-source reset: conflicting geographic labels and hierarchy labels require source-specific questions.
items.correctTeaching: OERp4 prose puts Upper Egypt south/upstream and Lower Egypt north/downstream; its Figure2 mouth label conflicts. Use the original satellite Figure1 only. Black Land is fertile Nile land; Red Land is desert. The teacher pyramid’s bottom label is Unskilled workers; the mystery separately asks about enslaved people. Do not silently merge the diagrams.
items.parentAction: 13 source-backed replacement chapters and all24 vocabulary terms are available. Project rubric images now reviewed. Orange-book149–151, older course files and teacher-media playback remain incomplete; unverified content does not supply scored answers.
